title: Standard publication front end in core, and a multi-tenant Papyrus service
description:
Planning only (drafted 2026-11-07 from the design memo `standard-frontend-memo.md`; Ryan's decisions of 2026-11-07 are binding). Successor to the closed initiative PPY-bcfd2d: the projector is shared; this initiative promotes the publication layer above it (layout, cards, nav, design tokens, brand) into Papyrus core and runs it for many tenants.

Decisions that shape every child:
1. Multi-tenant SaaS is the default tier. This reverses "a separate backend per site" (docs/standard-site.md section 0) for the default tier only. A dedicated AWS-account deployment stays an option: the same artefact with one fixed tenant, one front-end codebase for both.
2. One set of design tokens authored natively at the sizes people see. No multiplier, no dual stylesheet; the scaler is retired.
3. One ordering rule for every list: rolling seven-day buckets, newest bucket first; quality within a bucket; the most recent wins a tie; sections are placed by their best item under the same rule.
4. Threat Intelligence goes first and must run with no site hooks and no change to Machines on Machines code.
6. Shared-plan tenants never run their own code. Hooks exist only on dedicated deployments, and every hook in use is a tracked gap to promote into core.
7. v1 customisation: name, logo, colours (light and dark), allow-listed fonts, sections, nav, home template. Text floors, one image ratio on a 4px rhythm, contrast, no borders and colour-safe marks are platform policy for every tenant.
8-10. No free plan and no trial. Custom domains are in every plan. Pricing is by usage metered through Prospectus (the Anthus CRM and central account service, with its billing model in Prospectus docs/BILLING.md); no per-seat or per-agent pricing.
11. Tenants own 100% of their content; our code is open; our value is operating and improving it. Said in strong plain language in terms, docs and p.apyr.us.
13-14. Shipped, Anth.us and Machines on Machines stay dedicated for now. Threat Intelligence is not in that list: it is the first tenant of the shared stack, once it passes the brand-neutral acceptance test on the standard layout and real tenant authorisation has landed (our own pre-production site, so the safe first tenant). Distinctive Mark is dedicated pending its upgrade (open question, not decided by Ryan). Papyrus manages upgrades for dedicated customers; people who clone and run it themselves are on their own.

Standing rules: no arbitrary caps; indexes over scans; derived work computed once on change; DynamoDB is the card catalogue and text lives in S3 (never text in DynamoDB); CloudFront purging costs money, so sites are eventually consistent with a TTL; one new GSI per table per release; Gherkin for every behaviour change; every feature epic ends with p.apyr.us documentation.

Existing issues linked, not duplicated: PPY-bcfd2d (closed predecessor), PPY-6a3735 (section names), PPY-c63f18 (concept ranking), PPY-3d26a0 (recency buckets), PPY-7f1e54 and PPY-ee02b8 (whole-corpus reads), PPY-409932 (cache strategy), PPY-1f68bf (image style profiles), PPY-1b83d3 (home page), PPY-49e9b5 and PPY-77bb3b (reader voting and steering), PPY-2bc3e8 (hosted MCP), PPY-a1e75a (Prospectus waits).

Done when: Threat Intelligence runs on the standard layout with no hooks, a staging tenant is served from the shared stack, a paid sign-up reaches a live site with no human step, and the docs state tenant ownership plainly.

Scenario: A second brand runs on the standard layout
  Given Threat Intelligence has only a brand pack, sections and pages
  When it is built with the shared Gherkin suite
  Then it passes with no site Python or CSS and no Machines on Machines file changed

(f) site as data and brand pack: epic PPY-f8ec52 (with PPY-31efef, PPY-2a44b2), tasks PPY-1252ce PPY-e572de PPY-413576 PPY-91fb68 PPY-b21340 PPY-272c84
(g) dogfood migration: epics PPY-fe8bc6 and PPY-4f5fb1, tasks PPY-e1d26f PPY-e51189 PPY-0c4b55 PPY-16f13a PPY-8ca9a7 PPY-13fbea PPY-297ebe
(h) reader features in the shared tier: epic PPY-149b82, tasks PPY-6b084f PPY-5219fc PPY-d0a3d5 PPY-1f83a6
(i) governance and docs: epics PPY-84abde and PPY-02227e, tasks PPY-f7ce77 PPY-4a79f9 PPY-3ff465 PPY-7438d9 PPY-bd73b2

Does multi-tenant need big API schema changes? No big change to the shape of existing operations. Additive: optional tenantId on 52 tenant-owned models (55 of 60 models lack it today; the 3 identity models UserProfile, UserIdentity and PublicHandleClaim stay global), six new models as new tables, one new query (previewSitePage). Data, not schema: global index key values get a "<tenant>#" prefix, so no tenant index per existing index (Reference already has 15 indexes, 16 with PR #1239, of DynamoDB's default 20). New indexes: one tenantId index on each of about nine tables that have no index reaching all of a tenant's rows. Breaking, staged last: removing the global group rules on the shared stack (PPY-bdc4ee) and making tenantId required (PPY-b99fc0).

| Milestone | Entry | Exit | Customer-visible | Index deploys |

ReferenceIntake scan), PPY-d647ee, PPY-3fd0aa at 1 tenant; front-end track PPY-c446fe, PPY-2a44b2, PPY-31efef | lower cost; sites unchanged or better | Reference.publicFeedKey (PR #1239), per site, alone |
| M2 Tenant data foundations, additive (PPY-37c5df) | M0 (overlaps M1) | tenantId everywhere, new models, tenant keys, adoption tools, claims, tenant rules beside group rules, functions take tenant from caller | nothing | new tables only + PPY-1ce06f (one tenantId index per listed table, one release, never Reference) |
| M3 Isolation enforced on staging shared stack (PPY-6cb791) | M2 | PPY-daf673 staging, storage, workers, no guest API, no subscriptions, suite blocking, group rules removed (PPY-bdc4ee), tenantId required; security gate 1; release gate on | nothing external | none |
| M4 Shared serving + site as data (PPY-667a23) | M3, M1, PPY-7e396d passed | bucket prefixes, host routing, subdomains, freshness rules, shared newsroom host, SiteConfig/BrandPack/render from store, fair queue; two API-created test tenants served; load test passed; runbooks rehearsed | internal test tenants on staging | none |
| M5 TI on the shared stack (PPY-486592) | M4 + TI custom domain | rehearsal, cut-over, ops move, 14 days green | TI readers: no change; TI editors: shared newsroom | none |
| M6 Metering + spend ceilings (PPY-a36a7a) | M4 (parallel to M5) | metering events, spend gate, platform usage report, adaptive throttling, cost model | operators only | none |
| M7 Provisioning, lifecycle, export/delete, reader features (PPY-dad077) | M5, M6, Prospectus changes deployed | paid sign-up to live site with no human step in staging (PPY-e54eca) | staging sign-up | none |
| M8 First outside paying tenant (PPY-cf9039) | M7, Stripe live in Prospectus | external security review; terms + ownership statement; docs and p.apyr.us pages | public sign-up | none |

Earliest milestone at which Threat Intelligence runs on the shared stack: M5. Parallel and outside the milestones: dedicated sites adopt their fixed tenant one at a time (PPY-13fbea); managed upgrades (PPY-297ebe); Distinctive Mark's staged upgrade.

comments.text:
Milestone effects of Ryan's decisions of 2026-11-08 (launching a site is a data change only; lifecycle rule accepted; overage billing wanted; one shared Google client; public sites at <site>.p.apyr.us):
- M0 adds: Prospectus asks filed (PPY-966ef5 one 'papyrus' product with data deployments, PPY-6cb44b revise kanbus-8e3174 and build lifecycle events kanbus-6efecd, PPY-8a3c6a overage billing) and the design-partner decision PPY-37f2ec.
- M1 adds (now, parallel): PPY-25e0d7 cost accounting tags and token reports on our dedicated sites, then on the design partner's three sites at launch. This is the first real test of Prospectus cost accounting (kanbus-bb0b6c).
- M4 adds: PPY-fdbbd7 shared sign-in (one pool, one shared Google client, fixed callbacks, newsroom.p.apyr.us). Default subdomains become <site>.p.apyr.us (PPY-82de58).
- M6 now depends on PPY-25e0d7: metering goes through the Prospectus SQS sender library, not the quota usage route (live for Babulus only).
- M7 now also needs PPY-966ef5 (Prospectus data deployments; without it a shared-tier site would still need a reviewed file entry and a deploy), PPY-6cb44b (lifecycle events) and passes only after PPY-1da916 (security review of data-driven provisioning). M7 is the earliest point a design-partner site can launch on the shared tier.
- Design partner's three sites: recommended to launch DEDICATED now with cost accounting (PPY-37f2ec), and move to the shared tier after M7 with the TI runbook.
- After M7 (optional): PPY-496c0b bring-your-own Google client, after spike PPY-8eca5b.
- Unchanged: TI's earliest shared-stack point is still M5; first outside paying tenant still M8 (overage billing PPY-8a3c6a is not a launch blocker; the weekly quota stop is the default).
